title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on 8x RTX PRO 5000 72GB, TP8+EP8, prefix cache disabled: C1-C64 short/long plus 32K prefill

hardware.interconnect: PCIe only, no NVLink; GPU0-3 NODE within NUMA0, GPU4-7 NODE within NUMA1, cross-group SYS
hardware.topology_summary: nvidia-smi topo -m: 4+4 split across two CPU sockets
hardware.cpu_numa: 2 x Xeon Platinum 8488C, 192 threads; GPU0-3 -> NUMA0, GPU4-7 -> NUMA1; 1.5 TB RAM

software.clocks: not locked; default application clocks (idle 180 MHz, max 3090 MHz); 300 W power cap

model.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (538B-class MoE, 40 layers, 384 routed experts / 6 active, MLA attention with Engram tables)
model.quantization: FP8 block 32x32 weights (ue8m0 scales) + FP4 packed experts (expert_dtype=fp4); 476 GiB on disk

workload.input_tokens: 256 (short) / 8192 (long) / 32768 (ctx32k) requested. Measured prompts average ~120 / ~4,744 / ~16,520 tokens: random-ids is re-tokenized through the chat template, so the effective length is 47-58% of nominal even with the radix cache disabled
workload.output_tokens: 128 (short, ctx32k) / 256 (long) requested; the model stops at EOS after ~47 / ~119 tokens. The cap is not reached and ignore_eos does not change it on this build
workload.sampling: temperature 0, top_p 1.0, seed 42, one warm-up request per level
workload.server_notes: TP8 + EP8, --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4, dsv4/flashmla attention, --chunked-prefill-size 2048, --disable-radix-cache, --max-running-requests 32, --mem-fraction-static 0.85, --context-length 32768, CUDA graph decode bs<=32

commands.server: sglang serve --model-path /models2/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-cfg0 --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --ep-size 8 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --chunked-prefill-size 2048 --disable-radix-cache --max-running-requests 32 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32 --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 16 --context-length 32768 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8200  (env: HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True, NCCL_BUFFSIZE=2097152, SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=1, SGLANG_DSV41_TORCH_PREFILL_INDEXER=1, SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1)
commands.client: python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang-oai-chat --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8200 --model <local path> --tokenizer <local path> --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len {256|8192|32768} --random-output-len {128|256} --num-prompts {16 | 2*concurrency} --max-concurrency {1,4,8,16,32,64} --seed 42 --disable-tqdm

variance.note: Three independent server launches (container replaced between runs, weights reloaded). Long-request levels reproduce within a few percent; short-request levels at c4-c16 still spread widely, and c8 reproduces as an outlier in every launch - so this is a property of the stack, not of prefix caching.

methodology: Three independent launches with --disable-radix-cache. Each level is one benchmark invocation; metrics are client wall-clock; TTFT/TPOT come from streaming responses. Results are means of the three launches, p99 TTFT is the worst observed.
transferable: With prefix caching disabled, this box serves ~345-379 tok/s short-request output at c32-c64 and ~220 tok/s long-request output at c64
32K-context prefill is the expensive path: C1 output is 15.1 tok/s with a 1.9 s TTFT, and throughput only reaches 22.7 tok/s at c4 - prefill, not decode, sets the ceiling
Long-request levels reproduce across launches; short-request levels do not (see not_transferable)
not_transferable: The c8 short-request level is an outlier in every launch (see variance): do not read the short-request curve as a configuration result without repeating it
Effective prompt length is 47-58% of nominal because random-ids is re-tokenized through the chat template; verified with radix cache disabled, so this is not a caching artefact
Output length is model-determined (~47 / ~119 tokens); ignore_eos and min_tokens do not force the cap on this build
Compared with the cache-on dataset, long-request aggregate throughput at c4 drops from 154.5 to ~101 tok/s: prefix caching is worth roughly a third of long-request throughput on this workload
